Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2, a hosting platform). This is a WRITE task — make real code changes, going to production soon. Match the existing codebase's precise, deliberate style (it explains WHY in comments, tersely, not WHAT).

**Fix 1 — Migration can silently fake a successful transfer.**
Read `worker/migrate.ts` in full first, especially the `REAL_MIGRATION` constant (around line 14-20: `const REAL_MIGRATION = process.env.ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION === "1" && !SANDBOX`) and `runMigration` (around line 736-827). Currently, when `REAL_MIGRATION` is false (env var unset), the function runs a pure simulation — sleeps, writes fabricated log lines, sets `status: "DONE"`, and notifies the customer "Migration to {target} completed" — with ZERO indication anywhere (log, DB row, customer notification) that it was simulated, not real. This is a known, already-documented risk (see `docs/AUDIT-24H.md` if it still exists, for context only — don't need to read it, just know this is intentional legacy behavior being tightened, not removed).

Add a code-level safeguard so a missing/misconfigured `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION` flag fails LOUDLY instead of silently faking success, while preserving the SANDBOX simulation path (`!SANDBOX` check) since that one IS supposed to simulate safely for design/demo purposes and must keep working exactly as before. Specifically: if `SANDBOX` is NOT set (i.e. this is meant to be a real/production environment) but `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION` is also not set to `"1"`, this is a MISCONFIGURATION, not an intentional sandbox — the migration should fail with a clear error (e.g. mark the migration job `FAILED` with an error message like "Real migration is not enabled on this server — contact support" and notify the customer of a FAILURE, not fabricate a success) rather than falling through to the same simulation code path used for sandbox. Preserve exact current behavior when `SANDBOX=1` (simulate, as today). Read the surrounding code carefully to implement this as a clean early branch, matching the file's existing structure and error-handling conventions (look at how other failure paths in the same file mark a job FAILED and notify the customer, and replicate that exactly).

**Fix 2 — "My Services" is empty for domain-only or email-only customers.**
Read `lib/nx/services.ts`'s `listServices()` function in full. It currently queries `Server`, `HostingAccount`, and `FreeMinecraftServer` Prisma models but never queries `Domain` or `EmailSubscription`. Add both: query the current user's `Domain` rows (status ACTIVE, or whatever the equivalent "real, owned, currently active" filter is elsewhere in the codebase — check `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx` or similar for the standard query shape) and `EmailSubscription` rows (status not CANCELLED, matching the pattern in `app/dashboard/email/page.tsx`), and map each into the same return shape (`ServiceRow` or whatever the existing return type is called — read the file to find it) that Server/HostingAccount/FreeMinecraftServer already use, so they render identically to everything else on `/dashboard/services`. Include a real preview/icon (reuse whatever icon convention the file already uses for other service types — check `SvcIcon` usage, likely "domains" and "email" icon names already exist per other code in this session), a real status badge, and a real link to the item's own detail page (`/dashboard/domains/${id}` and `/dashboard/email`).

**Fix 3 — Hosting price display drift.**
Same file, same function: hosting rows currently show `renewalCents: h.plan?.priceCents ?? null` (the raw monthly list price) instead of the actual per-cycle renewal charge, which factors in the annual-term discount and any extra-disk surcharge. Find the REAL renewal-price calculation this platform already uses — check `worker/product-renewals.ts`'s `hostingRenewalPrice` function (or similarly named) — and reuse/call that same logic (or the underlying pure function it's built on, if calling the whole renewal-sweep function isn't appropriate for a read-only display context) so the displayed number matches what will actually be charged. If the real calculation function isn't easily reusable in a page context (e.g. it has side effects meant only for the worker), extract just the pricing math it uses into something callable from both places, OR replicate the exact same formula inline with a comment explaining it must stay in sync with `worker/product-renewals.ts`'s version — prefer actually sharing the function if you can do it cleanly without restructuring worker code you don't need to touch.

After each fix, run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` and resolve any type errors. Do not touch files outside `worker/migrate.ts` and `lib/nx/services.ts` (and possibly `lib/product-billing.ts` or similar if you need to extract a shared pricing function — keep any such extraction minimal and additive, don't restructure existing exports). Do not commit — leave changes unstaged. Report back file-by-file with line numbers and a plain-English summary of each fix.

The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). Never skip this because a daily timer already ran — the daily timer isn't synced to the moment you're about to change something. - **Stop and report before proceeding if a step turns out more destructive or irreversible than expected** — e.g. `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` reporting it would actually drop a column or table rather than just add one, a schema change that isn't purely additive, or anything that would disrupt a customer mid-session in a way the sanctioned scripts don't already account for. "Automatic" covers the routine, expected path; it does not mean an unexpected destructive step gets waved through. - **Anything outside the build/deploy/promote workflow is still stop-and-ask** — touching customer credentials, hand-editing `/opt/nxeon` outside the sanctioned scripts, restarting a service those scripts don't themselves restart, or touching any of the `/opt/nxeon-*` siblings that belong to other sessions. The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run a manual, ad hoc build in `/opt/nxeon`.** Clobbering its `.next` with a raw `npm run build` has taken the admin panel down before. Running the sanctioned `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Reaching node-1" above) is fine — it exists specifically to update production without that failure mode; improvising your own build command in that directory is not. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

## Summary

All three fixes are implemented and `npx tsc --noEmit` passes clean (exit 0). Nothing committed, all changes unstaged.

### Fix 1 — `worker/migrate.ts` (lines 620–644)
Added a misconfiguration guard between the `phase === "tls"` early-return and the "Fresh start" simulation entry point:

```ts
if (!SANDBOX && !REAL_MIGRATION) {
  const lastError = "Real migration is not enabled on this server — contact support.";
  await db.migration.update({ ... status: "FAILED", ... }).catch(() => {});
  await clearSecrets(migration.id, items).catch(() => {});
  await notify(migration.userId, `Migration to ${targetName} failed`, lastError, "/dashboard/migrate");
  return;
}
```
This fires only when `SANDBOX` is unset (a real environment) *and* `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION` isn't `"1"` — exactly the misconfigured case. It replicates the catch block's own FAILED/clearSecrets/notify pattern verbatim rather than inventing a new one. `SANDBOX=1` is untouched (guard short-circuits false), and `REAL_MIGRATION=true` is untouched (guard short-circuits false), so both existing paths behave exactly as before.

### Fix 3 — hosting price drift (done first since Fix 2 depends on it)
- `lib/product-billing.ts` (+23 lines): added exported `hostingRenewalPrice(acct, liveAnnual, perGbCents)`, moved verbatim from `worker/product-renewals.ts`, importing `extraDiskCentsAt` from `./extra-disk`.
- `worker/product-renewals.ts`: removed the local (unexported) duplicate definition, added `hostingRenewalPrice` to its existing import from `../lib/product-billing`, dropped the now-unused `extraDiskCentsAt` import. The one call site (`chargeHostingRenewal`) is unchanged.
- `lib/nx/services.ts`: hosting row's `renewalCents` now calls `hostingRenewalPrice(h, prices.annualDiscountPct, prices.extraDiskPerGbCents)` instead of `h.plan?.priceCents ?? null`. Widened the `prices` computation gate from `paid.length > 0` to also include `hosting.length > 0` (and `emailSubs.length > 0`, see Fix 2), since hosting/email pricing needs `annualDiscountPct`/`extraDiskPerGbCents` even when the customer has no paid VPS.

This was a deliberate, minimal relocation (not a restructure) — the function's signature, body, and only call site are unchanged; it just now lives in the shared pure module both callers already import from.

### Fix 2 — `lib/nx/services.ts` (+139/-… lines)
- `ServiceKind` extended to `... | "domain" | "email"`.
- Added `db.domain.findMany({ where: { userId, status: "ACTIVE" }, ... })` and `db.emailSubscription.findMany({ where: { userId, status: { not: "CANCELLED" } }, include: { emailPlan: true }, ... })`, matching the filters `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx` and `app/dashboard/email/page.tsx` already use.
- Two new mapping loops push `ServiceRow`s: domain → `href: /dashboard/domains/${id}`, `renewalCents: d.renewPriceCents ?? d.priceCents` (the frozen renewal quote, not first-term price), `termMonths: termYears * 12`; email → `href: /dashboard/email`, `renewalCents` computed via the same term-aware primitives (`productTermRenewalCents`, `emailMonthlyBaseCents`, `subscriptionTermMonths`, `frozenProductAnnualPct`) that `worker/product-renewals.ts`'s `emailRenewalPrice` uses, so it isn't a second ad hoc formula either.
- `normalizeStatus` gained two cases for `TRANSFER_PENDING`/`TRANSFER_FAILED` (DomainStatus-only values that previously degraded to the ugly generic fallback "Transfer_pending").
- `STOCK_PREVIEW` gained `domain: "/nx/hero-domains-globe.webp"` (real existing hero art) and `email: "/nx/svc/email.webp"` (no dedicated wide plate exists for email, so it falls back to the real service-mark asset rather than a fabricated placeholder).
